# Model runtimes (area `runtimes`)

Codex, Claude Agent SDK and API adapters behind one interface; pinned runtime versions.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **RUN-1** (agent): A provider's HTTP refusal says a plain cause from the status code first, then the provider's words (api.http_cause). Runtime errors point at Settings → AI, never at a `ferb` command or config.toml.
- **RUN-400** (owner): FERB keeps Codex, the Claude Agent SDK, and its own loop over the Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini APIs, each fixed. Core output schemas are provider-neutral so any adapter can run any role. Each is live tested on real calls one by one (Codex, Claude SDK on the owner's subscription, Anthropic API and Gemini API on the owner's keys); the OpenAI API is checked offline only until the owner has a key.
- **RUN-401** (owner): The owner runs tests/security/test_planner_injection_real.py once after the rebuild; if it passes, the Codex planner's stable per-role cache key (`[runtimes] codex_planner_cache`) is on by default. Until then it stays off. It works with the smaller prompts: caching reuses their stable part.
- **RUN-402** (agent): Supervisor (one-turn) Codex runs set `model_auto_compact_token_limit` out of reach, so an over-window prompt comes back as an overflow. Codex workers keep Codex's automatic compaction: a long tool loop compacts rather than fails (owner question T-404).
- **RUN-403** (agent): The planner's `worker_type` is a string checked against the runtimes available now; an unknown one goes back to the planner's repair loop naming the available types, and the dispatcher is told once and asked again. Worker types live in the planner's fixed Layer 1. Nothing blames config.toml.
- **RUN-404** (agent): ferb/runtimes/catalog.py `CATALOG` is the one list of runtimes: name, default model, sign-in kind, billing, factory, limits. A runtime is available only when its model is set and FERB's own sign-in or key is present; every former list (and `ferb setup --key`) reads it. Prices stay per model in prices.py, shared by Codex and the OpenAI API. Model defaults live only here.
- **RUN-405** (agent): Codex runs only on the app-server path with every model-visible extra disabled (`DISABLED`), a locked model catalog (`CATALOG_LOCKDOWN`), a read-only sandbox with approval never, a tool-catalog check of the request trace that fails closed, and an item gate that stops a run on an unexpected item or server→client request, recording kind, tool and server. Any new tool Codex offers is a stop.
- **RUN-407** (agent): The Codex MCP config sets `startup_timeout_sec` 120 and `tool_timeout_sec` 7 days; FERB's stall watchdog and stop end real hangs. Codex's version check and the locked catalog run once at daemon start, the catalog rewritten only when Codex's own catalog file changes.
- **RUN-408** (agent): ferb/runtimes/schema_shape.py reshapes core schemas per provider and maps answers back before FERB's check. Anthropic API and Claude SDK: a nullable object becomes a list of at most one item, a nested nullable scalar an optional property while the 24-optional budget lasts, the rest stay unions (at most 16). Gemini: an enum holding null becomes anyOf. Core schemas in ferb/core never change for a provider.
- **RUN-409** (agent): A Claude SDK run uses FERB's own sign-in (never the owner's ~/.claude login), blanks inherited ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN/CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, passes the run token as a 0600 file (`FERB_RUN_TOKEN_FILE`) in an owner-only folder, runs the bundled Claude Code (`cli_path`, no `claude` on PATH; missing, the run is refused), and sets `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false`. Sign-out removes FERB's marker.
- **RUN-410** (agent): thread/start's `baseInstructions` is FERB's system prompt for every Codex run, workers included, with empty developer instructions, replacing Codex's coding-agent base prompt.
- **RUN-411** (agent): `ferb runtimes pins` only reports. A pin moves to the newest release at least two days old, checked offline (never ~/.ferb, a login or a model request). Codex: package.json, package-lock.json (`npm install --package-lock-only`, `npm ci`), CODEX_VERSION and INPUT_CHARS_SOURCE, spikes/01_codex_mcp/codex_run.py last. Claude: pyproject.toml, `uv lock`, SDK_VERSION and CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION. Then the suite, mypy, and live real tests (Codex `-m real`, one owner-run `-m real_claude`).
- **RUN-412** (agent): With HOME and CODEX_HOME temporary: `codex features list` against DISABLED (a new default-on feature that adds a model-visible tool joins it); `codex debug models --bundled` against CATALOG_LOCKDOWN and limits_for; `codex app-server generate-ts` old vs new against what codex_stream.py uses and the recorded test messages; `--print-startup-config --strict-config` with FERB's flags; the input cap; the trace format tooltrace.py reads. Strongest: the adapter against a local Responses stand-in under sandbox-exec, including a lockdown-off run that must stop.
- **RUN-413** (agent): Read Claude Code's changelog since the old version; find the behaviours claude_sdk.py names (cache breakpoints, tool search, the too-long text, the MCP idle timeout, the cost field, the structured-output subtype, the auth commands) in the bundled binary's strings. Strongest: `ClaudeRuntime._options` against a local Messages API stand-in, the CLI under sandbox-exec with only localhost and no Keychain, a made-up API key, comparing the request's tools and cache_control with the old CLI's.
- **RUN-414** (owner): When a worker's tool loop overflows the model's context window, Codex compacts the conversation and the worker carries on.
- **RUN-415** (agent): Every adapter attaches FERB's tools (Codex: the MCP shim with the token file; the Claude Agent SDK: the same shim; the API loop: the gateway bridge) to a worker run, and to a supervisor (one-turn) run only when it is given a run token: the planner's lookups (ORCH-516). A supervisor run keeps its own settings with them: low effort, no automatic compaction, a streamed typed answer, the cached planner thread. Codex's item gate and tool-catalog check allow exactly the FERB tools the run was given, in either mode.
- **RUN-416** (agent): With `codex_planner_cache` on, every planner turn resumes the fixed-id template thread (one prompt_cache_key per Mac, role, model). Only an owner's chat turn with stable and changing parts puts its stable parts in the developer role; any other turn (scheduled or watch, review M4) resumes it with empty developer instructions and its whole context in the user turn, journaling `runtime.cache_skipped` (request id, why). Pastes no longer refuse: implements the owner's 2026-11-04 "(b) pastes count as your words".
- **RUN-417** (agent): Codex's `modelNotFound` says its cause from files (codex_exec.model_refusal, never ~/.codex): the pinned Codex's shipped catalog lacks the model or an entry needs a newer client: needs a newer Codex (a FERB update); the pin knows it but FERB's login's model list (codex-home/models_cache.json) lacks it or wasn't kept: the ChatGPT plan doesn't include it (renew, or pick another service in Settings → AI); else a line blaming neither. Codex's words follow. A direct-API 404 says the model isn't offered to this key.
- **RUN-418** (agent): The direct-API loop marks an error `image` only from the provider's own shape: OpenAI's Responses API image codes (`error.code` in IMAGE_CODES, from openai-python response_error.py); Anthropic 400s in the shapes its own client calls image errors (Claude Code 2.1.310: "image exceeds"+"maximum", "image dimensions exceed"+"many-image", "Could not process image"). Google, Codex's CodexErrorInfo and the Agent SDK define no image error: those never mark one, and a real image refusal there fails with its own words.
- **RUN-419** (agent): Every adapter times each model call with ferb/core/timing.py CallTimer on an injected monotonic clock and adds `timing` to its usage event, whole ms and no content: runtime_ms (the call's begin to the provider request, only where the runtime shows it), ttft_ms (to the first output), generate_ms (first to last output), tail_ms (to the usage report), total_ms (their sum) and `by`. A call begins when its request is handed over or the previous call's tool result goes back.
- **RUN-420** (agent): A Codex start records `start_steps` (ms) in its run state on the runtime's clock: version, files, spawn (the app-server), initialize, thread_start or thread_resume, turn_start (no account step since RUN-422). A Claude Agent SDK start records options, connect (Claude Code ready) and query. The orchestrator copies them onto the run's timing as start_steps_ms (ORCH-526). Nothing else about the run changes.
- **RUN-421** (agent): Codex: a call begins at turn/start or a FERB tool's completion; its request goes out at its request trace line; its output is item starts, deltas and completions, timed when read, not when consumed; a usage report that follows a tool already run keeps the tool out of both calls. The direct-API loop: from its POST (a retry's wait counts as runtime_ms) through each streamed event; an unstreamed answer is one output. Claude Agent SDK: one usage per turn, so its timing covers the turn, tools included.
- **RUN-422** (agent): Codex sends no account/read before the thread. Its ChatGPT-only guard reads FERB's login file instead: ChatGPT tokens and no OPENAI_API_KEY or auth_mode apikey, else the start is refused as signed out with nothing spawned. A refreshed login is published when the request trace shows the request went out, and again at the run's end. A sign-in Codex refuses comes back as the turn's own error (CodexErrorInfo unauthorized, or a refresh-token OAuth code), marked signed_out for ORCH-315's message and offer.
- **RUN-423** (agent): `catalog.call_limit` gives one deadline across start and answer, applied by every adapter: none for the planner's call (ORCH-528) or a worker's, CALL_LIMIT_S (900 s) for other non-worker calls beside the silence guard. Every adapter reports a contentless `progress` event for output that hands nothing over (Codex's reasoning, commentary and item notifications; the Claude SDK's stream events and tool results; the API loop's stream events without answer text and tool results): life for the silence guard only; a retry still isn't.
- **RUN-424** (agent): The daemon keeps each runtime's availability (RUN-404) as last known: read at start, then again only after the owner's runtime or model change (runtimes.use, a one-tap switch, a model changed in config), a sign-in (Claude's finishing; the app's runtimes.status, which reads all afresh), a runtimes.check, or a call the runtime refused for its sign-in, which marks it unavailable (`runtime.signed_out`). No timed expiry. The Claude marker file and the API key read for the request itself stay.
- **RUN-425** (agent): When Codex compresses a run's conversation (a completed contextCompaction item, RUN-414), the adapter reports one `compacted` event with the context size the last usage report gave (context_tokens_before) and the model's window, when known; the shared run loop records it as a `model.compacted` span under that call's span, which `ferb trace --full` shows. Trace only: nothing else changes (no checker fact, no behaviour).
- **RUN-426** (agent): In a Codex run, an mcpToolCall item from server `codex` whose tool is list_mcp_resources or list_mcp_resource_templates is let through without a violation. read_mcp_resource and every other tool not FERB's still stop the run (RUN-405).
- **RUN-428** (agent): For RUN-431. A model the owner typed that FERB's tables don't document (anthropic_api, openai_api, google_api LIMITS; Codex's max output) is sized with the smallest context window and max output FERB documents for that provider, said in the limits' source, instead of being refused. A Codex model not in Codex's own catalog still can't run (Codex refuses it).
- **RUN-429** (agent): For RUN-431..433. runtimes.models gives a connection's models (an API key's live list from its provider's models endpoint with the stored key; Codex's catalog; Claude's documented ids), its model now and each role's own. runtimes.model saves a model only after a check: in the provider's list for that key, else one tiny call; on failure the old model stays and the provider's words come back. Saved to [models] <runtime>, a role's to [role_models] <role> = {runtime, model} (used only while that role runs there). Claude's default is claude-opus-5-5.
- **RUN-430** (agent): Anthropic's stream: a tool_use block whose argument fragments are empty or absent keeps its start's input (else {}); fragments that aren't JSON become the call's error ("not valid JSON"), told back to the model as the tool's result (its one repair, as for a non-object), and the turn is replayed with {} there. OpenAI's empty or blank arguments are no arguments. Gemini's arguments are already an object.
- **RUN-431** (owner): Settings → AI offers a model for each connection (ChatGPT, Claude, each API key), from the models it can use, and lets the owner type any model id; FERB checks a model before using it and keeps the working one when it fails.
- **RUN-432** (owner): A connection runs one model; an optional per-role model (planner, worker, checker) sits under Advanced, empty meaning the connection's model. Claude's sign-in defaults to Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5).
- **RUN-433** (owner): Settings → AI shows "<provider> key saved" for a key the Keychain holds (read for presence, never shown), gives it its own card (APP-792), never asks again for a saved key, and shows the model each connection uses with its picker. A Claude sign-in runs with its default model.
- **RUN-434** (agent): For RUN-435. runtimes.check_calls {runtime, model?} runs, through the connection's real adapter and model: a planner call with SUPERVISOR_SCHEMA and the planner's lookup tools offered; a worker call that calls check.ping (no arguments) and check.echo (an argument) and answers in WORKER_SCHEMA; a checker call in CHECKER_SCHEMA; a call with a 16 px generated PNG. Each line: pass or fail, the provider's words redacted, model, typed form, seconds, tokens, cost; and the total. The check tools exist only during the check and touch nothing.
- **RUN-435** (owner): Settings → AI's Check runs the same small set of real calls (planner, tools, worker, checker, a picture) on whichever connection is in use, costing cents, and shows each result; the owner runs it on Codex, Claude, the Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini keys, and before every release.
- **RUN-436** (owner): On the Anthropic API, FERB's instructions (tools and system) and the stable context, conversation history included, are cached with the 1-hour TTL; only the automatic tail breakpoint keeps the 5-minute TTL. Each call's usage records its cache writes by TTL and its cache reads, and 1-hour writes are priced at 2x input.
- **RUN-437** (agent): For RUN-436. The system block (and RUN-427's stated-format block) and content[cacheable-1] carry {ephemeral, ttl 1h}; the top-level automatic breakpoint stays 5 minutes, after them, as the API requires. A request whose last block is that 1h marker is sent without the top-level field (the API refuses a differing TTL there). Usage gains cache_write_5m_tokens and cache_write_1h_tokens (from usage.cache_creation; no split: all 5m); Price.cache_write_1h prices the 1h part.
- **RUN-438** (owner): FERB leaves OpenAI's cache lifetime at its default (30 minutes on GPT-5.6+; no prompt_cache_options set) and measures. Each call's usage records cache reads and cache writes as the provider reports them: OpenAI's cached_tokens and cache_write_tokens, Gemini's implicit cachedContentTokenCount; a write count the provider doesn't report (Gemini, Codex, older OpenAI models) is marked not reported, never taken as zero. GPT-5.6+ writes are priced at 1.25x input.
- **RUN-439** (owner): Each Check line is given up after the check tool's own fixed limit (LINE_LIMIT_S, 60 s; real calls keep none) with the provider's words, or "no answer after 60 s" plus what the provider answered meanwhile (a rate or usage limit, HTTP 429, with its retry-after). A 429 error says when it asks to retry. Results are kept per connection: the selected connection shows only its own last result, and a running check names its connection. The two tool-call lines say they ran inside the worker call.
- **RUN-440** (agent): For RUN-427, to measure the fallback live. The API loop's and Claude Code's usage report carries repair: "asked" (the stated answer was outside the schema and is told back), then "fixed" or "failed" on the answer after it; none otherwise. scripts/question_run.py counts per task and per run: calls by typed form, repairs asked, fixed and failed, the repair calls' seconds, and the planner's own repair turns and how many ended without error.
- **RUN-442** (owner): Supersedes RUN-441's GPT model; the rest of RUN-441 stands. The real-task run uses gpt-6.1-sol on Codex (the ChatGPT subscription) and the OpenAI API, claude-sonnet-5-5 on Claude Code and the Anthropic API; Google is not run; no cost cap from FERB's side; no payment is ever approved in the run; T-1060 waits until after the runs.
- **RUN-443** (owner): The live task run records, per turn and per task, the CPU and memory used by FERB's processes (its background service, everything it starts, FERB.app) and by each running browser, and says how much of it is the task's: FERB's own processes during the sequential run are the task's unless other FERB work ran beside it (listed), and browser figures are an upper bound that includes the owner's own browsing.
- **RUN-444** (agent): For RUN-443. Groups from ps (pid, ppid, rss, command): the daemon (-m ferb.daemon), its descendants, FERBNotch's tree, ferb.native_host, each browser's bundle and children. A group's CPU is the sum over its live processes of libproc's own CPU plus its ended, waited-for children's (MacReadings), at the turn's start and end, so short-lived commands count without sampling. A 2 s look keeps RSS and footprint peaks and the busiest children. Read-only from ferb.db: other task trees and resource_samples rows overlapping the turn. A failed ps or a daemon restart is reported, never zero.
- **RUN-445** (owner): Every model run of every role and runtime counts its wrong calls: a call to a tool the run wasn't offered, and a call FERB's gateway refused because the grant's calls were spent (the planner's lookups, ORCH-516). Lookups and tools that ran never count. At WRONG_CALLS_CAP (10) the shared run stops the run (ToolLoop) and records a model.tool_loop span. The planner then answers from one last call with no tools and what its lookups found (ORCH-558); a worker's attempt ends with the reason.
- **RUN-446** (agent): For PRM-334 and RUN-445 (answer_rules.py). Empty: no answer text and no tool call. The API loop and Claude Code send FOLLOW_UP once per run after the model's turn, kept as returned (Gemini drops a turn with no parts); a second empty ends the run marked `empty` (EmptyAnswer). A Codex turn completed with no answer is marked `empty`. Usage reports carry stop, blocks (kinds, never content) and follow_up (asked, fixed, failed). A tool the run wasn't offered is a tool_call with offered False. Refines RUN-440.
- **RUN-447** (owner): Supersedes RUN-427 for the planner where its form can't be enforced; the rest of RUN-427 stands (resend once without the refused format, remembered 24 h; over the counted limits stated from the start; a misfit told back once; `typed` on usage; other roles stated). In FERB's API loop (Anthropic API now; Gemini when its form doesn't fit) the planner is offered ferb_answer, a non-strict tool with the core answer schema, and PRM-336's line in place of the schema. Its call is the answer; a text answer still counts. OpenAI and Codex stay enforced; Claude Code keeps its own.
- **RUN-448** (agent): For RUN-447. ApiRuntime(planner=True) adds ANSWER_TOOL whenever it states the form, through each provider's without_format(state, statement, tool), never among the run's tool names: the gateway never sees it, it is never a tool_call (never a wrong call), and the last tool-free call keeps it. Its call's arguments are the answer; the reply's other calls don't run; a misfit gets repair_note as its result once. Stream parsers return its arguments as answer text and mark its start (a text_delta with restart: the draft restarts). Usage carries answer_via; question_run.py counts it.
- **RUN-449** (agent): Every Codex run gets `model_providers.ferb_chatgpt` and `model_provider = "ferb_chatgpt"` (codex_stream.provider_entry): what Codex 0.166.0's built-in `openai` provider resolves to for ChatGPT sign-in (name OpenAI, base_url https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, wire_api responses, requires_openai_auth, its version and organization/project headers), with supports_websockets false. Threads and the planner's template name that id; `_isolated` refuses any other. RUN-405, 410, 416 and 422 are unchanged.
- **RUN-450** (agent): Refines RUN-422, whose rule stands (no account/read; the ChatGPT-only guard reads the login file). Its evidence is corrected: Codex makes the workspace routing lookup (GET /backend-api/wham/accounts/check) itself at each thread's start and the turn's request waits for it, so removing account/read moved that wait from start_steps into the first model call's runtime_ms; it did not remove it. Taking the lookup off a message's path needs a Codex process started before the message (research; not built).
- **RUN-451** (agent): Refines RUN-426. A Codex mcpToolCall item whose tool is list_mcp_resources or list_mcp_resource_templates passes the item gate when its server is `codex` (a listing of every server) or `ferb` (the model asked for FERB's server by name): FERB's bridge offers no resources, so either lists nothing. read_mcp_resource on any server and every other tool not FERB's still stop the run (RUN-405).
